checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The piece is dense with exact, seductive textures early — the ads that 'cut off dead at the median,' the car 'gone gray — the color a thing turns when nobody argues with it anymore,' the building read 'bottom to top' like a scar history, the CramIt bar tasting 'like chocolate described to someone who'd never eaten food' — and these do pull the reader in with lived-in wrongness before horror arrives. But once the schism/mesh-intrusion plot takes over, the prose shifts almost entirely to procedural, bureaucratic rhythm (forms, clearances, timestamps, cost lines) and the sensory allure thins dramatically; the horror (the sound 'above his chair,' the locker, the thing in her mesh) lands mostly through clinical description and dialogue exposition rather than through the same seductive texture-work established at the opening.
checks.Fix: Sustain the material, sensory specificity established in the opening (smells, light, texture of decay and mismatch) into the mid-and-late sections so the horror of the schism and the mesh-intrusion arrives wrapped in the same strange-beautiful concreteness rather than receding into procedural/administrative exposition.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The opening paragraphs establish Yemina's commute as a routine ('ran the way it always ran... a machine that never stopped, only changed gears') and linger on infrastructural texture — the elevated train, ad emitters cutting off at the median, dueling permit offices — well before the missing-children plot is introduced through her caseload.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Most terms (Arcturus/Meridian, neuretics, Pilsen Veil, ArcSec, calibration print) are woven in through concrete sensory and procedural detail — 'Her neuretics were contractor-grade: district-issue mesh, grown in a public clinic eleven years ago' reads as natural bureaucratic interiority. But several proprietary terms arrive as unglossed proper nouns a newcomer can't place — 'GLMZ', 'AAMA', 'Class-3 site', 'the schism' are used many times before any orienting context is given, and phrases like 'a hazard classification' or 'schism proximity' assume the reader already knows what a schism is in this world.
checks.Fix: Give 'the schism' and 'GLMZ' a single early in-voice anchor (e.g., a line where Yemina's own thought defines the schism as the thing that opened wrong in the world, the way she defines neuretics and the seam) so first-time readers aren't left inferring the central phenomenon purely from accumulated context clues.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: 'GLMZ' appears repeatedly (e.g., 'no instrument in the GLMZ is pointed at,' 'every corp contract in the city' vs. 'across the GLMZ') with no in-voice expansion anywhere in the text; 'AAMA' is used freely on first appearance ('the Anomalous Activity Monitoring Authority')—which is properly glossed—but 'GLMZ' never receives the same treatment.
checks.Fix: Add an in-voice gloss at GLMZ's first appearance, e.g. 'no instrument in the Great Lakes Metro Zone—the GLMZ, everyone called it—was pointed at that frequency.'

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: The heater-cold moment ("Her shoulders drew up half an inch before she'd decided anything. Then she put them down. It was March. The lake was where it had always been.") is the closest thing to a human crack, but it's a physical/stoic reflex quickly re-armored, not a flash of who she once was outside her function; the kitchen-table arithmetic on her debt and the West Lawn recording memory are also filtered entirely through her investigator register rather than a personal register.
checks.Fix: Give her one beat—a memory, a name, a person outside the caseload—that surfaces without being immediately converted into case logic, so the reader glimpses Yemina before she was 'the contractor.'

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The node ends on a plot beat, not a landing: 'She had a name, and an address, and a count that was running, and behind her eyes something patient that wanted the same answer she wanted and had never once told her why. She did not check the queue again. There was nothing in it she hadn't already agreed to.' This is business concluding (case accepted) plus forward momentum into the next case, which is a hook/cliffhanger structure rather than a quiet closing gesture.
checks.Fix: After the acceptance and before driving off, give one small, contained, non-editorial physical gesture (setting the cold tea in the sink, locking the car, touching the notebook margin she never crossed out) that lets the reader feel the accumulated cost settle rather than propel forward into case 48.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: All four registered plants land as complete, functional beats on a first pass (the drone as ambient world detail with a clean diagnostic log, the blank sender field read simply as bureaucratic strangeness, the neuretics described as 'always slightly behind' explaining her professional competence, the 'careful margins' of the intruder's edits read as just another unsettling sensory detail) while each is built to re-signify once the ending recontextualizes it — e.g. 'CAPTURE SUSPENDED — SPECTRUM RESERVED... 17–19 Hz' functions as an in-scene obstacle on first read and only becomes 'someone closed a shutter the same morning something started using it' on a second pass.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The prose reads as a fully worked, self-contained investigative narrative with world rules (Arcturus/Meridian seam, corp contracts, schisms, psionics) explained in-scene through Yemina's procedural habits rather than exposition dumps; nothing suggests structural patchwork for newcomers, e.g. the calibration-print/tuning realization and the locker sequence are organic escalations, not bolted-on onboarding beats.

checks.Title: Orient through GLMZ's five pillars
checks.Evidence: Neuretics (leased vs corp-grade mesh, Φ90/month debt), CorpoNations (Arcturus/Meridian split jurisdiction, gray zones like the freight-yard locker handoff), and Schism-adjacent phenomena (the 17-19Hz signal, calibration prints, children 'crossing') are richly textured and systemic; but AIs as agentic factional entities are essentially absent — the reception android and voice menus read as bureaucratic set-dressing, not agents with stakes, and the 'thing in her mesh' is framed ambiguously as schism-adjacent rather than clearly identified as an AI faction actor.
checks.Fix: Give the entity riding Yemina's mesh (or another AI presence) explicit markers of agenda and factional identity — a name, a goal, a rivalry with another AI or corp system — so it reads unmistakably as an AI player in the setting rather than an unclassified schism effect.
